extracted.intended_audience: teachers and students in North Carolina public schools (teachers of North Carolina history)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and classroom organization for teaching a school textbook on North Carolina history, including lesson structure, use of visual aids, chapter questions, and required study of the State Constitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a wall map of North Carolina
rubrics_metrics.description: The teacher of North Carolina History will be greatly aided in the work by having a wall map of North Carolina before the class, and to this end the publishers have prepared a good and accurate school map, which will be furnished at a special low price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require the pupils to go to the map and point out localities when mentioned, also places adjoining; trace the courses of the rivers which have a historical interest, and name important towns upon their banks. A good, reliable wall map can be procured at a moderate price from the publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make chapters short so each forms one lesson
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been deemed proper to make the chapters short, that each may form one lesson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapters are intentionally concise to fit within a single class period; teachers should treat each chapter as a standalone lesson.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include chapter-end questions on main points
rubrics_metrics.description: At the close of each chapter will be found questions upon the main points of the lesson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These questions will furnish thought for many other questions which will suggest themselves to the teacher; use them to drive recitation and to prompt further inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use both visual and mental media (multimodal instruction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any subject can be more thoroughly taught when both the eye and the mind of the pupil are used as mediums for imparting the knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine visual aids (maps, wall charts) with oral recitation and mental engagement to deepen understanding; emphasize map work alongside textual study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplement textbook with local/state historical details
rubrics_metrics.description: There are many small matters of local State history which could not be included in the compass of a school book, but a teacher will be helped by referring occasionally to 'Moore's Library History of North Carolina.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce minor local facts when appropriate to enliven lessons; consult supplementary local histories to provide students with additional, regionally-relevant material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require study and analysis of the State Constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: The Appendix contains the present 'Constitution of North Carolina.' Then follows a series of 'Questions on the Constitution'... This is an entirely new and valuable feature in a school book, and contains an analysis of our State government. Teachers should require all their students of this history to read and study the Constitution and endeavor to answer the questions thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign the Constitution and its accompanying analytical questions as required reading/work; use the questions to ensure students understand the structure and functions of state government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate patriotism and pride in the State
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspire your pupils with a spirit of patriotism and love for their native State. A little effort in this direction will show you how easily it can be done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stories of state achievements and noble deeds to fix attention and awaken desire to learn more; intentionally foster latent feelings of pride to develop better future citizens.
